ctor.rationale: `base(1, CardType.Power, CardRarity.Uncommon, TargetType.Self)` (Automation.cs:18-21) == cost 1 / POWER / UNCOMMON / SELF. No keywords, no tags on either side.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new EnergyVar(1)` (Automation.cs:14) == `_energy_gain = 1`, read at the apply site as `DynamicVars.Energy.IntValue` (Automation.cs:25). `_energy_gain` is in `Card._MAGIC_ATTRS` (cards/base.py:185-189) so `magic_number` surfaces it, matching the game's single printed var.

OnPlay.rationale: `PowerCmd.Apply<AutomationPower>(choiceContext, Owner.Creature, DynamicVars.Energy.IntValue, Owner.Creature, this)` (Automation.cs:25) == `PowerCmd.apply(ctx.hooks, ctx.player, AutomationPower, self._energy_gain, applier=ctx.player)`. Self-target, self-applier. AutomationPower's every-10-cards-drawn counter belongs to the power stream. Presentation, folded in: ExtraHoverTips -> base.EnergyHoverTip (Automation.cs:16) is hover-tip wiring with no sim counterpart.

OnUpgrade.rationale: `EnergyCost.UpgradeBy(-1)` (Automation.cs:30) == `self._energy_cost = max(0, self._energy_cost - 1)` (1 -> 0). The upgrade changes the COST, not the EnergyVar -- the power's amount stays 1 on both sides. Downgrade-safe (`_init_vars` re-seeds both fields; `card_probes.py downgrade` does not list automation).

guards.what: no TriggerAnim call, unlike the other Power cards in this batch (Aggression.cs:18, Barricade.cs:22)
guards.rationale: Nothing to mirror; the sim has no animation layer either. Noted only because the asymmetry could look like a missing step.
